_meta.description: Forward-tuning overrides for manager_pitching='v2', active for any sim date >= 2026-04-14 via should_use_forward_tuning(). Each key below has its own provenance block. See Syndicate/mlb_sim_accuracy_assessment_and_optimization_plan.md Phase 1 item #1 for full context.

starter_hook_add_pitches.description: Re-fit of the starter-hook-add-pitches override for the MLB manager_pitching='v2' model, made necessary by promoting log5/odds-ratio combination for hr_tgt/inplay_hit in sim_engine/pitch_model.py (2026-07-19) -- that change shifted the raw pitch-count bias curve enough that the prior fit (-11, from 2026-07-17 against the naive-average combiner) no longer lands near zero. Re-swept manually against the same 35-tune/11-holdout 2026-season backfill (seed 2026, 100 sims/game), grid [-12,-13,-14] under the new log5 combiner, calibration disabled to see the raw effect. See the log5 combiner promotion note in pitch_model.py's _combined().
starter_hook_add_pitches.rationale: Clean, monotonic bracket: -12 -> holdout bias +0.73 (tune), -13 -> holdout bias +0.44 / essentially zero on tune (-0.02), -14 -> overshoots negative (tune -0.73). -13 lands closest to zero on both tune and holdout without overshooting, and is a materially better pitch-count fit than the prior -11 value ever achieved even under the old naive-average combiner (holdout bias was +1.35 at best).

previous_fit.context: Fit against the naive-average rate combiner (pre-log5). Grid [-14,-11,-8,-5,-2]. Superseded by this entry once log5 combination was promoted for hr/inplay_hit.

starter_hook_stamina_excess_weight.description: New tunable added 2026-07-20: sim_engine/simulate.py's _starter_effective_hook previously hardcoded a 0.25 weight on stamina above the manager's baseline hook -- min(base,stamina) discarded any excess entirely, then only 25% of it was credited back, while below-baseline stamina got full credit via the min(). This severely dampened upside for high-stamina workhorses (a maxed-out stamina_pitches=115 vs base=95 only reached eff_hook=100, barely above a league-average pitcher's 92), which combined with a real data-attribution bug in _derive_stamina_pitches_from_season_stats (season-total pitches divided by start count alone, corrupting estimates for mixed-role pitchers -- see build_roster.py fix same day) to make pitcher pitch-count projections converge toward a narrow band regardless of real ace-vs-back-end differences. Fixed the data-attribution bug directly in code; made the 0.25 weight tunable and swept it here since it's a genuine magnitude question, not a correctness bug. Swept grid [0.25,0.50,0.75,1.00] against the same 35-tune/11-holdout 2026-season backfill, on top of the stamina fix + the newly-populated Statcast player-feature set (see data/statcast/features/) + selective log5 + starter_hook_add_pitches=-13.
starter_hook_stamina_excess_weight.rationale: Clean monotonic tune-day trend crossing zero near weight=1.00 (0.25->-0.63, 0.50->-0.38, 0.75->-0.15, 1.00->+0.06), but holdout generalization favored 0.75 over 1.00 (holdout bias +0.20 vs +0.39, outs_mae 3.877 vs 3.914) -- the tune-day optimum didn't hold on holdout, so the more conservative value was selected. HR/hits/total-runs metrics stayed completely flat across the whole grid (hr_avg_p 0.0945-0.0946, full_mae_total_runs 3.539-3.548), confirming this change is cleanly isolated to pitcher workload with no side effects.

starter_quality_hook_weight.description: New tunable: eff_hook (_starter_effective_hook, above) is driven entirely by stamina_pitches -- a workload-history proxy -- with no channel at all for the starter's own pitching quality. Confirmed via real roster-artifact dump: Chris Sale (.336 K-rate) and Nick Martinez (.116 K-rate) both derived to stamina_pitches=89 on the same slate. A live pull-decision trace confirmed eff_hook does correctly drive real pull timing (corr 0.51 with actual pitch-count-at-removal), ruling out the mechanism itself -- it's purely a missing-signal problem. _starter_matchup_hook_adjustment already gives the *opposing* lineup's quality this kind of influence; _starter_quality_hook_delta (sim_engine/simulate.py) gives the pitcher's own quality the same, using K-BB% (K-rate minus BB-rate, a standard sabermetric quality proxy) rather than raw K-rate. A first cut using raw K-rate deviation from a fixed constant, hand-tuned by weight, was tested at weight=0.7 and 0.35 across the full 46-date/1210-start backtest and found real but badly miscalibrated (overshot elite into over-projection, made mid-high tier *worse* at every tested weight). Root-caused via OLS regression of real per-start outs bias against K-BB% (n=1210): corr=-0.236, R^2=0.056, zero-crossing 0.307, slope -15.29 outs/unit -- replaced the hand-tuned formula with these fitted coefficients directly (starter_quality_hook_reference/_slope/_max_pitches, left at their code defaults; only the weight is promoted here).
starter_quality_hook_weight.rationale: At weight=1.0 (applying the fitted regression directly, capped at max_pitches=10), all four market-line tiers moved the correct direction or stayed flat -- elite -0.416->-0.462 outs bias (flat), mid-high +0.993->+0.732 (improved, the tier that got *worse* under every hand-tuned attempt), mid +2.125->+1.782 (improved), back-end +3.035->+2.659 (improved). Modest magnitude (closes ~12-26% of each tier's gap), consistent with the weak individual-pitcher R^2 -- most per-start outs variance is real game noise, not pitcher quality -- but safely and correctly shaped, unlike the discarded hand-tuned version. Full-game side effects are small and consistent with the other hook-related promotions above (brier_home_win 0.2224->0.2241, mae_total_runs 3.742->3.771, mae_run_margin 3.323->3.365).

discarded_first_attempt.description: Raw K-rate deviation from a fixed 0.223 constant, hand-tuned by weight instead of fit to data.

starter_tto_quality_scaling.description: _starter_tto_quality_mult (sim_engine/simulate.py) scales pull_starter_third_time_penalty (the flat, per-team 3rd-time-through-order penalty) by the starter's own K-rate. It has TWO consumers: the pull-probability logit in _select_pitcher_v2 (tested first, part 3, and found to have no measurable real-scale effect on outs) and a K/BB/HR/inplay RATE-degradation multiplier in _adjust_pitcher_day_rates_v2 (simulate.py:1936) that was never separately isolated -- every starter's simulated K-rate gets knocked down by the same flat amount once fatigued past bf>=18, elite arms included, even though real aces are known to hold their stuff better through the order. The part-3 test (weight=0.5, 12 dates, before k_combine_log5_weight or starter_quality_hook_weight were promoted) was underpowered by the same margin that made the K-rate combiner itself look like a dead end at 12-16 dates before the full 46-date/882-start test revealed a real corr=0.283 signal -- re-tested at full scale on top of the three already-promoted fixes.
starter_tto_quality_scaling.REVERTED_2026-08-01: Promoted to 1.0 first (see 'superseded_rationale'), then reverted the same session once tested against the betting-accuracy harness properly -- part 11's test was stacked on top of the already-reverted inplay_hit_combine_log5_weight=0.0 state; retested stacked on the correct (inplay=log5) happy-place checkpoint instead (full46_baseline_v2 vs full46_happyplace_test, n=882 pooled hit rate): strikeouts 55.78%->54.65% (WORSE -- this is the exact market the fix was built to help, via the K-rate decay mechanism, and it made real-money accuracy worse there), hits_allowed 54.63%->56.43% (better), outs 59.54%->59.15% (slightly worse). Net effect across the three markets is roughly a wash at best, and it degrades the one market it specifically targeted. Given the session's core lesson (statistical-bias improvements do not reliably translate to betting-accuracy improvements -- see inplay_hit_combine_log5_weight's REVERTED note above), a fix with mixed/ambiguous real-money evidence and a per-tier statistical benefit of only ~2-3% doesn't clear the bar. Reverted to 0.0 (unconditional no-op, reproducing pre-session behavior exactly).
starter_tto_quality_scaling.superseded_rationale: Real, small, consistently-signed STATISTICAL effect confirmed at n=882: all four market-line SO tiers moved the correct direction (elite -2.618->-2.555, mid-high -1.131->-1.100, mid +0.161->+0.147, back-end +0.827->+0.789), and elite outs bias improved meaningfully (-0.422->-0.202). One blemish: mid-high outs bias worsened slightly. Full-game side effects flat. This looked like a clean, safe, small win until graded against real betting outcomes in the correct (non-confounded) context.
